Bench · Raspberry Pi 4 · IMX219

Camera arm assembly

Seventeen steps: rotating base, spring-balanced shoulder, elbow, head with tilt and rotation, electronics box with power supply and lid carrying the Raspberry. All printed parts are PETG. M3 button-head screws with hex socket (2 mm key), except the M8 bearing pins and the M2 screws of the MG90S and camera. LCD display and remote controller are optional and have their own guides.

new parts in the stepalready assembledinsertion direction

Printed parts

The arm needs items 1-12: fixed base, turntable, turret, electronics box, upper arm, forearm, elbow support, head base, cradle, camera plate, small parts (pinion, spacer, small ring, yoke, 2 rollers), lid with cable clamp. Items 13 (display box) and 14-15 (controller) are optional.

Hardware and components

M8 pins (bearing axles)

  • M8×60 hex head bolt — 1
  • M8×40 hex head bolt — 1
  • M8 self-locking nut — 2
  • M8 washer — 2

M3 button head (ISO 7380, 2 mm key)

  • M3×8 — 2 (KY-024)
  • M3×10 — 10 (motor 2, MG996R tabs 8)
  • M3×12 — 7 (turret 4, tilt pin 1, cable clamp 2)
  • M3×16 — 5 (elbow pin 1, lid 4)
  • M3×25 — 2 (head)
  • M3×30 — 1 (springs)
  • M3×35 — 2 (elbow)
  • M3×50 — 2 (rollers)

M3 nuts

  • M3 nut — 9 (plate 4, elbow 2, head 2, springs 1)
  • M3 self-locking nut — 2 (rollers)

Other screws

  • M2 supplied with the MG90S — 4
  • M2×6 — 4 (camera)
  • M2×6 self-tapping — 4 (ULN2003)
  • M2.5×4 screw from the Freenove kit — 4 (breakout)
  • M2.5 nut — 4 (in the breakout posts)
  • 4×25 countersunk wood screw — 8 (to the bench)

Mechanics

  • 608 bearing — 3
  • 7×51 spring — 2
  • 0.5 mm cord — about 30 cm
  • 6×3 neodymium magnet — 1
  • Velcro strap — 2

Motors

  • 28BYJ-48 + ULN2003 board — 1
  • MG996R with round horn — 2
  • MG90S with its horns (single for the tilt, cross for the rotation) — 2

Electronics

  • Raspberry Pi 4 in a GeeekPi Armor case
  • Camera v2 IMX219 + ribbon cable 50 cm or longer
  • WS2812B 24-LED ring
  • KY-024 Hall module
  • Freenove FNK0080 breakout + 40-pin male-female GPIO cable (20 cm)
  • 4 Forbox terminals
  • 2 × 1000 µF 35 V capacitors (in parallel)
  • PCA9685 16-channel I2C + 4 M2.5×8 screws
  • 1 × 330 Ω resistor (in series on the LED ring)
  • 5V 5A power supply (85×58×32)
  • 230V rocker switch (19.2×12.9 hole)
  • 3×0.75 mains cable with plug
  • Official Raspberry Pi 5.1 V 3 A USB-C power supply

Wiring

  • Servos → plugs into the PCA9685: channel 0 shoulder, 1 elbow, 2 tilt, 3 rotation (the + comes from the V+ terminal)
  • PCA9685 → SDA → GPIO2, SCL → GPIO3, VCC → 3V3, GND → GND, V+ terminal → +5V terminals, GND terminal → GND terminals
  • GPIO17 / 27 / 22 / 23 → ULN2003 IN1 / IN2 / IN3 / IN4
  • GPIO24 → KY-024 DO
  • 3V3 → KY-024 VCC (3.3 V only)
  • GPIO10 → 330 Ω in series → LED ring DIN
  • GND (breakout) → GND terminals: common ground required
  • +5V terminals → power supply +V, capacitors +, PCA9685 V+, ULN2003 +, LED ring 5V
  • GND terminals → power supply −V, capacitors −, PCA9685 GND, ULN2003 −, KY-024 GND, LED ring GND, breakout GND
  • Breakout 5V → do not connect: the Pi has its own power supply
  • Raspberry Pi → official 5.1 V 3 A power supply in the USB-C socket, not from the terminals; the common ground goes through the breakout GND

Steps

STEP 01 / 17

Fixed base

fixed baseM8×60 hex bolt28BYJ-482 M3×10 screwsKY-0242 M3×8 screws
  1. Insert the M8×60 bolt from below: the hex head goes into its seat and can no longer turn.
  2. Place the 28BYJ-48 with the shaft facing the centre and fix its two ears on the posts with 2 M3×10 screws.
  3. Screw the KY-024 onto the pedestal with the Hall sensor facing the centre, under the magnet track. Bend the sensor legs upwards: its face must sit 3-5 mm below the plate.
  4. Fix the base to the bench with 4 countersunk 4×25 wood screws.
The wood screws can still be reached later, but now it is easier.
STEP 02 / 17

Pinion

17-tooth pinion
  1. Slide the pinion onto the shaft from the round-hole side: the shaped section at the top grips the flats of the shaft.
  2. Lay a 0.5 mm piece of card on the motor collar, push the pinion down until it touches it and remove the card.
  3. The bottom of the pinion stays 2 mm above the motor flange and does not rub on the collar.
The round hole in the first 2.5 mm is there because the 28BYJ-48 shaft has flats only in the last 6 mm: before, the pinion sat too high and jammed the plate.
STEP 03 / 17

Turntable

turntable2 × 608 bearingsspacer6×3 magnet4 M3 nuts
  1. Press a 608 into the upper seat (disc side) down to the chamfer.
  2. Turn the plate over: slide the spacer into the hub, then press the second 608 into the lower seat.
  3. Glue the magnet into the seat under the disc with a drop of cyanoacrylate.
  4. Put the 4 M3 nuts into the hex seats under the disc; a drop of glue holds them in place.
The KY-024 senses one pole only: if the sensor does not trigger during testing, flip the magnet.
STEP 04 / 17

Turntable on the base

assembled turntablesmall ringM8 washerM8 self-locking nut
  1. Slide the turntable onto the M8 bolt, meshing the ring gear with the pinion.
  2. Add the small ring, the washer and the self-locking nut.
  3. Tighten until the plate has no vertical play but still turns freely by hand.
Turn the plate one full revolution: the magnet must pass over the sensor and the plate must not touch the trimmer and components of the KY-024.
STEP 05 / 17

Shoulder turret

turret608 bearing2 rollers2 M3×50 screws2 M3 self-locking nutsM3×30 screw + nut
  1. Press the 608 into its seat from the inner side of the bay, against the outer lip.
  2. Place rollers A (above the axle) and C (behind) between the side plates and insert the M3×50 screws from the bearing side.
  3. Close with the self-locking nuts without locking the rollers: they must turn.
  4. Fit the M3×30 screw between the cheeks at the bottom, in the middle one of the three holes.
STEP 06 / 17

Turret on the turntable

assembled turret4 M3×12 screws
  1. Place the turret on the plate with the rollers on the side opposite the notch on the plate edge: the notch shows where the arm points.
  2. Screw the 4 M3×12 screws into the nuts already inserted in the plate (2 mm hex key).
The central hole of the turret lets you reach the M8 nut of the base with a socket wrench.
STEP 07 / 17

Upper arm and shoulder pin

upper arm (humerus)M8×40 hex boltM8 washerM8 self-locking nut
  1. Place the arm between the side plates with the hub aligned with the bearing and the horn seat facing the servo window.
  2. Through the servo window insert the M8×40 bolt: the head goes into the hex seat of the arm, the shank into the 608.
  3. From the outside fit washer and self-locking nut. Tighten lightly: the arm must rotate freely.
STEP 08 / 17

Shoulder servo

round hornMG996R4 M3×10 screws
  1. Bring the MG996R to mid travel (1500 µs) with a servo tester or from the electronics box.
  2. Slide the round horn into the gap between arm and side plate and screw it into the arm seat, reaching through the window with the screwdriver.
  3. With the arm at mid travel, about 70° from vertical, insert the servo through the window with the shaft in the horn.
  4. Fix the tabs with 4 M3×10 screws driven directly into the plastic.
Do not fit the central horn screw: the axle is held by the M8.
STEP 09 / 17

Springs and cord

2 × 7×51 springsyoke0.5 mm cord (about 30 cm)
  1. Hook the lower end of the two springs onto the M3 screw between the cheeks.
  2. Slide the yoke onto the upper ends.
  3. Tie the cord to the central hole of the yoke, run it over roller C, over roller A and tie it to the central hole of the arm (28 mm from the axle).
  4. With the arm vertical the springs must be just under tension.
If the arm drops by itself use the 32 mm hole or lower the M3 screw; if it tends to rise use the 24 mm hole.
STEP 10 / 17

Elbow support

elbow support2 M3×35 screws2 M3 nuts
  1. Slip the support onto the end of the arm until it stops.
  2. Insert the 2 M3×35 screws from above (head in the counterbore) and close with the nuts in the hex seats underneath.
STEP 11 / 17

Forearm and elbow servo

forearmround hornMG996R4 M3×10 screwsM3×16 screw
  1. Screw the round horn into the hub seat of the forearm.
  2. Slide the forearm into the support bay.
  3. With the servo at mid travel and the forearm in line with the arm, insert the MG996R through the window with the shaft in the horn.
  4. Fix the servo tabs with 4 M3×10 screws.
  5. Turn the elbow round: on the side opposite the servo the support side plate has a hole in line with the hub (second image).
  6. Screw the M3×16 screw in there: it grips the side plate and enters the hole of the forearm hub, which turns on it like on a pin.
Screw the pin in until the head touches the side plate, without forcing: the forearm must turn freely by hand.
STEP 12 / 17

Head base

head base2 M3×25 screws2 M3 nuts
  1. Slip the head base onto the tip of the forearm until it stops.
  2. Fix it with 2 M3×25 screws from above and the nuts in the seats underneath.
STEP 13 / 17

Cradle and head servos

cradleMG90S rotationMG90S tiltsingle horn4 M2 screws supplied with the servosM3×12 screw
  1. Insert the rotation MG90S into the cradle FROM THE FRONT, bottom and cable first, through the window of the small plate: the tabs rest in front of the plate. Fix it with 2 M2 screws and route the cable out through the notch in the window.
  2. Place the single horn in the hub seat of the cradle (hub in the round recess) and fix it with 2 small screws in the holes of the arm: they enter the slot under the arm and grip the sides.
  3. Put the cradle into the head base bay.
  4. With the servo at mid travel and the cradle in line with the forearm, insert the tilt MG90S through the window and fix it with 2 M2 screws.
  5. From the opposite side screw the M3×12 pin into the side plate up to the cradle hub.
STEP 14 / 17

Plate, camera and LED ring

camera platecross horn4 small horn screwsservo central screwWS2812B 24-LED ringcamera v2 IMX2194 M2×6 self-tapping
  1. Place the cross horn in the seat on the back of the plate (hub in the round recess, long arms horizontal) and fix it with 4 small screws inserted from the front through the slots, into the holes of the arms.
  2. Put the LED ring in the seat on the front with the LEDs facing forwards, towards the camera side, and route the 3 wires (5V, DIN, GND) through the holes to the back.
  3. With the rotation servo at mid travel, push the plate onto the shaft with the camera upright.
  4. From the front, through the hole in the middle of the boss, screw in the servo central screw: it locks the plate on the hub.
  5. Screw the camera onto the 4 standoffs with the lens facing outwards and the ribbon coming out of the slot at the bottom: it covers slots and central screw, so it is fitted last.
The central screw now also goes through 1.6 mm of plate: if the supplied one does not reach the shaft use an M2×8. The camera ribbon runs all the way to the Raspberry: you need a ribbon of at least 50 cm.
STEP 15 / 17

Complete arm

final checks
  1. Run the servo cables, motor cable, camera ribbon and ring wires along the arm and forearm and secure them with cable ties: tighten well on the ribbon too, so it does not slip.
  2. Leave a soft loop at each joint, so the cables do not pull at the end of travel.
  3. Before powering the servos, move each joint by hand over its whole travel and check that nothing snags.
STEP 16 / 17

Electronics box

box5V 5A power supply230V rocker switchcable clamp + 2 M3×12Freenove FNK0080 breakout + 4 M2.5×4 screws + 4 M2.5 nutsPCA9685 + 4 M2.5×8 screwsULN2003 + 4 M2×64 Forbox terminals2 × 1000 µF 35 V capacitors4 × 4×25 wood screws
  1. Screw the box to the bench with 4 wood screws through the ears, next to the arm base, with the cable exit slot facing the arm.
  2. Fix the power supply to the bottom with your own screws, terminal block towards the centre of the box.
  3. Snap the switch into the hole in the front wall, pass the mains cable through the round hole and secure it with the cable clamp and 2 M3×12 screws.
  4. Wire the mains: live → switch → L of the power supply; neutral → N; yellow-green earth → ⏚. Heat-shrink on the spade terminals.
  5. Insert an M2.5 nut into the side seat at the top of each of the 4 posts, then screw on the Freenove breakout with the M2.5×4 screws from the kit. The ULN2003 module takes 4 M2×6 self-tapping screws.
  6. Screw the PCA9685 onto its 4 posts with M2.5×8 self-tapping screws, servo pin rows towards the power supply. Next to it is the seat for the BSS138 level shifter: it is only needed if you fit the LCD display (separate guide).
  7. Put the 4 Forbox terminals on their anchors (2 for +5V and 2 for GND, joined in pairs with a short piece of wire) and secure them with cable ties; connect +V and −V of the power supply and the two 1000 µF capacitors in parallel (+ on 5V).
  8. Make the connections in the «Wiring» table: the 4 servo cables come in through the slot in the right wall and plug into channels 0–3 of the PCA9685; motor, KY-024 and LED ring through the same slot.
Work on the 230 V side only with the plug pulled out. Before printing, measure with a caliper the holes of the ULN2003 module (uln_foro) and of the PCA9685 (pca_fori) and correct them in electronics_box.scad.
STEP 17 / 17

Lid and Raspberry Pi

lid4 M3×16 screwsPi 4 in Armor case2 Velcro straps40-pin male-female GPIO cablePi power supply 5.1 V 3 A
  1. Connect the 40-pin GPIO cable to the breakout connector and route it through the rear slot of the lid.
  2. Close the lid with 4 M3×16 button-head screws into the corner posts. The round hole in the lid, above the ULN2003, is for the LCD display wires if you fit it.
  3. Place the Pi case in the cradle with the GPIO side towards the slot and secure it with two Velcro straps through the slots.
  4. Connect the other end of the 40-pin cable to the Pi GPIO (pin 1 to pin 1, red wire on the pin 1 side) and plug the cable of its power supply (5.1 V 3 A) into the USB-C socket; it passes through the hole next to the cradle.
To reopen the box, first remove the straps and unplug the 40-pin cable from the Pi.
